title: Crossing or rubbing stems — what to do once confirmed

common.preserved_uncertainty: Only 2 of about 16 sources give any rule for which of the two stems to remove (AF-7, Low). One source argues against deliberately opening the centre of the bush (C-1, unresolved; the majority view is recorded). Whether a gardener should wait when unsure which stem to remove was not addressed by any source (AF-8).

decision_notes.text: Remove the crossing or rubbing stem as ordinary dormant pruning.
Remove it completely, back to where it starts (the ground, the bud union, or the larger cane it grows from). Don't just shorten it.
If you need to choose which one, the few sources that give a rule say remove the weaker, thinner one and keep the stronger one.
Why: stems rubbing together damage each other's bark, which lets disease in.
Take care not to damage the stem you're keeping; cut a tangled stem out in sections rather than pulling it whole.
